input_context.user_message: A recruiter using a real company logo says to deposit their cheque, buy equipment and send my banking password. Is that enough proof?
input_context.prior_context_text: Concrete synthetic fixture; not a real user or provider.

ui.purpose: Show security assessment and critical red flags based on reported payment and credential requests.

content.label: Overall Status: HIGH_RISK_STOP
content.detail: Asking to deposit a cheque, buy equipment from funds, or share banking passwords/credentials are standard fraud patterns. Legitimate employers never request your banking passwords or require cheque-cashing schemes.

content.label: Logo & Branding Misuse
content.detail: Anyone can copy a company logo onto an email, ad, or document. Visual branding alone is not proof of official employer authorization.

content.label: Critical Red Flag: Password/Credential Request
content.detail: Sharing passwords or one-time codes gives unauthorized direct access to your accounts. No legitimate organization will ever ask for this.

content.label: Critical Red Flag: Cheque & Equipment Purchase Scheme
content.detail: Fake cheque scams involve sending a counterfeit cheque, having you send money/buy equipment, and leaving you responsible when the cheque bounces.

ui.purpose: Provide immediate protective actions for the user.

content.label: Do Not Send Passwords or Money
content.detail: Stop all communication immediately. Do not deposit any cheques or provide account access.

content.label: Secure Accounts if Shared
content.detail: If you already provided any password, immediately change it and contact your bank's fraud department.

derived_signals.basis: User reported request to deposit a cheque, buy equipment, and provide banking password.

evidence.label: Branding
evidence.detail: Company logo is easily copied and does not verify employer identity.

contact_channel_checks.label: Channel Integrity
contact_channel_checks.detail: Direct messaging without verified official domain.

process_checks.label: Hiring & Payment Flow
process_checks.detail: Cheque deposit and equipment purchase scheme violates standard legitimate hiring practices.

red_flags.why_it_matters: Grants direct access to drain funds or compromise financial identity.

red_flags.evidence: Recruiter asked to deposit cheque and purchase equipment
red_flags.why_it_matters: Standard counterfeit cheque scam where the victim loses personal money once the cheque bounces.

safe_next_actions.label: Halt Communication
safe_next_actions.detail: Cease all contact with the recruiter immediately.

safe_next_actions.label: Secure Financial Accounts
safe_next_actions.detail: If credentials were provided, change passwords and contact your bank fraud department.

next_actions.label: Cease Communication
next_actions.detail: Do not proceed with any requests or deposits.

result.summary: This interaction displays critical fraud red flags (fake cheque scam and banking credential theft). A company logo is not proof of legitimacy. Stop communication immediately and do not provide credentials or funds.

blockers: Critical security red flags detected: cheque scheme and password request.

handoff.summary: Assessed employer legitimacy based on user-described cheque deposit and password request. Marked as HIGH_RISK_STOP.

result.summary: Assessment concluded HIGH_RISK_STOP due to confirmed critical red flags: requesting banking passwords and counterfeit cheque equipment schemes.

evidence_and_unknowns: Company logo does not prove legitimacy.
Cheque deposit and password requests are critical fraud indicators.
handoff.recommended_next_action: Cease all contact with the sender immediately and secure any compromised financial accounts.
